[USER] User inquired about the probability of winning three games in a row in a game where a number is drawn between 1 and 10.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The probability of winning three games in a row is calculated as (1/10) * (1/10) * (1/10) = 1/1000, or 0.001.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] If the game is played 1000 times, one would expect to win three games in a row approximately once.  
[USER] User asked about the probability of winning twice if the game is played four times.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The probability of winning exactly two games out of four is calculated using the binomial probability formula with k = 2, n = 4, and p = 1/10.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The formula used is: P(exactly 2 wins) = (4 choose 2) * (1/10)^2 * (9/10)^2 = 6 * (1/100) * (81/100) = 486 / 10000 = 0.0486.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The probability of winning exactly two games out of four is approximately 0.0486, or 4.86%.  
[USER] User inquired about the probability of winning exactly one game out of four.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The probability of winning exactly one game out of four is calculated using the binomial probability formula with k = 1, n = 4, and p = 1/10.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The formula used is: P(exactly 1 win) = (4 choose 1) * (1/10) * (9/10)^3 = 4 * (1/10) * (729/1000) = 2916 / 10000 = 0.2916.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The probability of winning exactly one game out of four is approximately 0.2916, or 29.16%.
